gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each budget rapid trigger board costs per key, or that the $3.20 step from the wired to the tri-mode Gamakay NS68 buys wireless at 1,000 Hz (a 1 ms report interval) instead of the 8,000 Hz (0.125 ms) the listing title advertises.
standout_why: Compared against mechanicalkeyboard.net, setupinsider.com, keyboardverdict.com and gamepadsquire.com, all opened 2026-11-21. mechanicalkeyboard.net already states the 0.125 ms report interval at 8,000 Hz and simple price steps between boards. None computes price per key, counts rapid trigger settings, compares scan interval with report interval, or covers the NS68 at all. The two cited pages (PC Gamer's Hall effect guide, RTINGS' rapid trigger research) returned only navigation text, so I could not check them; PC Gamer names the NS68 and may carry part of this. If it does, standout drops to 1.
decides: The four maker-store prices read today sit within $5.70 of each other ($36.79 to $42.49), so price alone does not separate them. On derived figures the wired Gamakay NS68 leads: it has the lowest cost per key ($0.54), 68 keys with arrows for $3.20 less than the 61-key Redragon K617 HE, and a 0.01 mm rapid trigger step against the Redragon's 0.1 mm. That supports the NS68 wired as the pick or a top-three place. The tri-mode NS68 should not be sold on 8K: Gamakay states 1,000 Hz in wireless. The MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro ($37.40 from-price) remains the 60% rival; its per-key figure is left out because its key count could not be read.
